page: Vultr vbm-8c-128gb-amd is a dedicated bare-metal server powered by an eight-core, sixteen-thread AMD EPYC 4345P processor operating at a 3.9 GHz base frequency. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this instance features 123.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory clocked at 6 GHz, offering roughly 7.71 GB of RAM per virtual thread. Storage is provided through an integrated 3890 GB NVMe SSD array, while hardware accelerators such as GPUs are absent. Network connectivity includes one complimentary public IPv4 address, and hardware-level virtualization is supported via AMD SVM.

Benchmark results highlight exceptional single-thread processing capabilities, with both stress-ng single-core execution and Geekbench single-core scoring inside the top decile. In compression tasks, single-threaded gzip and bzip3 decompression both register top-tier throughput. In contrast, aggregate parallel scaling aligns with median values; multi-core stress-ng, Geekbench multi-core, and PassMark CPU metrics place in the middle 50% percentile due to the eight physical core count. Memory performance shows top-tier scores in PassMark memory testing and solid cached read throughput, though sustained large-block uncached write bandwidth settles into the lower quartile at 21.89 GB/sec.

From an architectural standpoint, the server delivers high resource density by combining top-tier per-core clock rates with ample DDR5 memory and nearly 3.9 TB of direct-attached NVMe storage. Because computing resources are fully dedicated without hypervisor overhead, it minimizes latency variance and noisy-neighbor interference. The hardware configuration makes this server suited for database workloads, in-memory caching systems such as Redis, build automation, data transformation pipelines, and lightweight CPU-bound inference for small language models.
description: Vultr vbm-8c-128gb-amd is a dedicated bare-metal server configured with an 8-core, 16-thread AMD EPYC 4345P processor running at 3.9 GHz. Accompanied by 123.0 GB of DDR5-6000 RAM and a fast 3890 GB local NVMe SSD, it operates on the x86_64 architecture without hardware GPU acceleration. In synthetic benchmarks, the machine achieves top-tier single-core performance across Geekbench and compression utilities, while multi-core metrics sit comfortably within median distributions due to its dedicated 8-core count. The combination of high single-thread clock speeds, robust memory capacity of approximately 7.71 GB per thread, and multi-terabyte direct-attached NVMe storage makes this server well balanced for intensive database operations, memory-resident caches, CI/CD compilation, and standalone web serving environments requiring consistent dedicated throughput.
